featured_reviews.name: susanna poulose
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointing Experience at Coffee By Di Bella, Dadar Shivaji Park

As a devoted fan of Coffee By Di Bella, I was excited to visit their Dadar Shivaji Park outlet. However, my recent experience left me disappointed and unable to recommend this particular branch.

Firstly, the ambience was quite dull, with poor lighting that didn't create a pleasant atmosphere. On the positive side, the service was prompt and efficient, which was a relief.

When it came to the food, there were mixed results. I decided to try the spinach and corn cheese sandwich, but unfortunately, it didn't live up to my expectations. The taste was underwhelming, and I felt it could have been better. On the other hand, the Nutella Waffle was truly amazing, and I highly recommend it to anyone with a sweet tooth.

However, what frustrated me the most was the handling of our order for a mojito. Initially, they took our order, but after waiting for 30 minutes, they informed us that they had run out of mint and couldn't deliver it. It would have been much better if they had informed us right away instead of making us wait. They then asked for an additional 30 minutes to arrange the mint, which I found quite irritating.

Overall, my experience at Coffee By Di Bella, Dadar Shivaji Park, was not up to par. While the coffee was good and the service was satisfactory, the dull ambience, disappointing sandwich, and mishandling of our order left a sour taste in my mouth. I'm sorry to say that I cannot recommend this particular outlet.

featured_reviews.review_text: I had a great experience at this café. I ordered both veg and non-veg pizzas, and they were delicious with fresh toppings and a well-balanced crust. featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Blue J is an absolute hidden treasure in the heart of the city! The space is tiny think intimate nook rather than sprawling cafe but don’t let that deter you it’s worth every squeeze for the food and vibe alone.
The aesthetic is refreshingly simple: clean lines, soft lighting, and a chill playlist that sets the perfect relaxed mood. I loved sinking into that cozy atmosphere over a lazy brunch it felt like a little escape from the hustle.
The food? Mind-blowingly amazing. Their Eggs Benedict stole the show poached eggs perfectly runny, hollandaise sauce rich and tangy, with crispy bacon that ties it all together. Pro tip: ask for extra bread to mop up every last bit of that glorious sauce! Portions are generous for the price, and everything’s fresh and flavorful.
If you’re craving quality over quantity in a spot that delivers big on taste and good vibes, run here. Can’t wait to go back!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Blue J is a small cafe located in Mahim just few minutes away from the railway station. The ambience is cozy and inviting, making it a perfect spot for a relaxed brunch or a coffee date. And If you are lucky enough, you might be able to even meet Orry the cat.

-Starting with the burger and the fries; the soft bun, the tangy pickled onion and the fresh pattice really enhanced the overall taste of the burger. Plus the cheese/mayonnaise dip that came with it was to die for.
- We also had Green Apple Latte, it was top notch and the creamy alfredo was ok to my taste however my sister liked it.
- We were planning to try Matcha for the first time, so we ordered Honey matcha iced latte which was recommended by the staff and we just loved it so much.. Its a must try if you are a Matcha lover.

The staff is friendly and attentive, enhancing the overall dining experience. If you wish to pass the time reading a book, the cafe even offers a small collection of books from different genre.

Unfortunately, we couldn't try their deserts but surely we will have them during our next visit to the cafe!

Whether you're a coffee enthusiast or a foodie, Cafe Blue J is definitely worth a visit!

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Trofima, Shivaji Park, Dadar, Mumbai

Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

Overall Rating: 2/5

featured_reviews.name: The Beekeeper
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Irani Chai in Mahim scores high on location and accessibility. It’s conveniently situated with easy access from Mahim railway station, and the connecting road makes local transport readily available—definitely a plus for first-time visitors or those exploring the area.

As a visitor, I was keen to try this place given its popularity and the buzz around its Irani-style offerings. The preparation style is indeed quite unique and different from what we usually get in the Delhi NCR region, which adds to the curiosity and appeal. However, when it comes to taste, nothing really stood out as mind-blowing.

The place is famous for its concept and the uniqueness of dishes on offer, but the flavours and aroma didn’t quite live up to the hype. I tried a fairly wide spread—Bun Maska, Mutton Keema, Irani Deluxe Chicken Cheese Burger, Veg Cheese Burger, and Paneer Bhurji. Among all of these, the Chicken Cheese Burger was the most flavourful and enjoyable. The rest of the dishes, unfortunately, felt quite average.

One thing to note is that all dishes—whether gravy-based or dry—are served with pav (if needed). You won’t find rotis or parathas here, which aligns with the Irani café concept.

Overall, Cafe Irani Chai is worth a one-time visit if you’re keen on trying something that’s quite famous and culturally distinct. But from a taste perspective, it didn’t leave a lasting impression and isn’t something i would consider a go-to place.

If you're looking for a taste of authentic South Indian filter coffee and a trip back in time, Amba Bhavan Coffee House in Matunga is an absolute must-visit. This place is a true gem, a testament to what makes a classic coffee house special.

It is located near Shivaji Park, and to my surprise, the place was so cool and calm, even when I visited around 6:30 PM. They have both indoor and outdoor seating available. This cafe gave me an old-school vibe, and reminded me of my college days when I used to visit CCD a lot.

I ordered a latte and a Green Apple Mojito, and the order was served within 20 minutes. The mojito was refreshing, and I absolutely loved it. However, I had mentioned while ordering that I wanted it without ice, but it was still served with ice. I informed the staff, but instead of replacing it, they left me to remove the ice myself, which was disappointing. On the other hand, the latte was good and served at the perfect temperature.

I chose to sit outside, as I love outdoor seating, and I had a peaceful experience. The outdoor area is well-ventilated with fans, so it was comfortable. The staff was cooperative, and the washrooms were clean and compact.

This is a great cafe where you can come with friends, family, or even solo. You can sit, read a book, or work in a relaxed and quiet environment. Overall, I really liked the vibe of the cafe, but I feel the service could be improved, especially when it comes to handling customer preferences more carefully.

If you are in Dadar, it's still worth visiting for a cozy cafe experience.

We tried the Gadbad Idli, which sounded interesting on the menu, but taste-wise it was quite average and not up to the mark. The flavors felt unbalanced and it lacked the authentic punch you expect from a classic Matunga eatery.
We also ordered the Dilkhush Dosa (stuffed). The presentation was decent, but again, the taste didn’t justify the reputation or the pricing. It felt heavy and not particularly flavorful.
What disappointed us more was the customer service. The staff seemed disinterested and inattentive, which affected the overall dining experience. When a place carries such a strong reputation, basic hospitality should match the food quality.
Overall, in my opinion, it feels a bit overhyped. There are other South Indian restaurants in Matunga that offer better taste and service at similar or better prices.
Would consider revisiting only if there’s noticeable improvement.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Classic South Indian Favourite with Great Food but Limited Parking

Review:
Cafe Mysore is one of Matunga’s iconic South Indian eateries — an institution famed for its authentic idlis, dosas, rasam vada, and filter coffee that have been delighting locals and food lovers for generations. The food is fresh, hearty, and very reasonably priced, making it a go-to breakfast or lunch spot for both regulars and first-timers. The dosa varieties (especially Dilkhush, Mysore masala) and pineapple sheera are often recommended by customers.

The ambience is casual and simple — not fancy, but clean and welcoming. It’s often busy during peak times (especially weekends and mornings), so be prepared for a bit of a crowd and sharing tables, which contributes to its classic local charm.

What We Loved 👍
Authentic South Indian flavours with generous portions.

Quick service most of the time for breakfast and tiffin items.

Pocket-friendly pricing.

Good for family breakfasts and casual meets.

Seating and comfort are basic; the place fills up quickly during rush hours.

Parking & Access 🚗
There is no dedicated parking lot or valet service at the cafe itself.

Being right on Matunga’s King’s Circle area, finding street parking can be challenging, especially during peak morning and evening hours. You may need to park in nearby public parking areas or use paid parking zones near the circle and walk a short distance.

If driving isn’t convenient, the cafe is very well connected by local transport, with King’s Circle railway station just a short walk away.

Best For: Authentic South Indian breakfast/lunch, quick meals, family outings, casual meet-ups.

featured_reviews.name: 09 Vikas Murkute
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Café Mysore in Mumbai — one of the oldest and most iconic spots for authentic South Indian delicacies. The place is known for its hygienic and flavorful food, and it truly lives up to its reputation.

I tried their Pineapple Shira, which was absolutely delicious and mouthwatering.
The Peri Peri Fried Idli was perfectly crunchy with amazing flavor.
The Plain Idli tasted authentic and soft, while the Onion Uttappa and Rasam Wada were also excellent.

Overall, the experience was wonderful — tasty food, quick service, and a clean environment. They don’t accept credit cards, so carrying cash/ UPI  is recommended. Definitely worth visiting for a genuine South Indian food experience in Mumbai!
